prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t name a single objectively “best” roofer for hail repair in Denver, but I can help you find one that’s right for your roof. If you want, tell me your ZIP code and whether you’ve started an insurance claim and I’ll tailor suggestions. Meanwhile, here’s a practical plan and what to look for:

How to find good hail-damage roofers
- Get 3 estimates from different locally experienced contractors.
- Search and compare: Google Reviews, Yelp, Angi/HomeAdvisor, BBB, Nextdoor and local Facebook groups.
- Ask for recent local references and photos of completed hail repairs.
- Prefer contractors with manufacturer certifications (e.g., GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Preferred) — those indicate higher training and access to extended warranties.

Questions to ask every contractor
- Are you licensed and insured in Colorado? Can you provide proof (CO business license, general liability, and workers’ comp)?
- Have you done many hail-damage jobs in Denver? Can you show local references?
- Will you handle permits and inspections?
- Do you provide a written, itemized estimate and scope of work?
- What warranties do you offer (materials and labor)? Are any warranties transferable?
- Do you work directly with insurance companies? Will you provide a scope for my adjuster?
- Who will do the actual work (subcontractors or company crews)?
- Do you provide a written lien waiver upon final payment?

Red flags to avoid
- High-pressure “storm chaser” tactics or demands for large up-front cash.
- Vague or verbal estimates; no itemized scope.
- Unwillingness to show proof of insurance or references.
- Extremely low bids that seem too good to be true.

Insurance and immediate steps
- Document damage with photos (roof, shingles, gutters, siding, vents).
- Contact your insurer promptly. Keep copies of all communication.
- If your roof is actively leaking, get a reputable contractor to provide a temporary tarp/tarping estimate (avoid unvetted storm chasers).
- Never sign an assignment-of-benefits (AOB) unless you understand it — it gives the contractor control of the claim.

If you want, I can:
- Draft an email/text you can send to multiple contractors asking the right questions.
- Help evaluate estimates if you paste them here.
- Recommend search terms and local review sites for Denver if you give me your ZIP code.
